correctness.rationale: Every side updates a color 0,1,2 via a deterministic map depending only on whether the opposite side contains an excited color 1. Consequently the ordered pair of nonempty color supports maps to another such pair in a finite 7x7 quotient independently of a,b. Enumerating the 49 transitions yields only closed support configurations: both-zero fixed, both-full supports with actual period three, and a two-support alternating class with actual period four; all other pairs have first-entry depth <=4. Within each closed class the vertex-level map is a permutation on colors, so macro periodicity and actual microperiod coincide after checking these classes. For side size a, the counts of assignments to exactly one/two/three named colors are 1, 2^a-2 and 3^a-3*2^a+3, respectively. Summing products over the 49 support cases gives the ten displayed polynomial formulas, their sum exactly 3^{a+b}, and cycles of lengths three and four counted by their periodic states. A completely separate enumeration of all 49 quotient types and symbolic formulas and all 810 labelled states for a,b in {(2,2),(3,3)} was completed; uniformity rests on exact support factorization, not sampling.
residual_risks: The result assumes both graph parts nonempty and deterministic synchronous threshold-one transition (not probabilistic updates).
The 49-case finite quotient is the exhaustive proof for arbitrary graph sizes; direct small-graph enumeration is corroborative only.
